title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the clay oven. Keep it, take the brass door, or re-roll.

options.label: The clay oven
options.lineage: A tandoor seen straight on, from a dim room
options.thesis: Dinner is a look into the oven: the dish sits in the opening, the name is the sign above it.
options.viewport: The name and directions are sign-sized on the dark surround. A large circular opening holds one dish on a flat coal field, with a short ranked list of the others beside it.
options.risk: A circle crop of food can read as a pizza-oven gimmick if the clay wall is not a real field of color.

raised.raise: The opening is a full field of color and is the state of the chosen dish, not a tint on a photo.
The clay wall is one unbroken color, and the dishes rank as a short list in one corner.
The name and the way in are the largest structure on the page, not a small header button.
Hours, phone, and ordering each occupy one calm place and show “not yet confirmed” as the reading.
The visit block is a place, with the address as its furniture, not a contact form.

options.label: The brass door
options.lineage: A hotel door plate, the number doing the talking
options.thesis: 4213 is the monument. The menu is what is served behind that door.
options.viewport: The numerals 4213 fill the left of the first screen. Bombay Palace and a single directions action sit in the brass. The selected menu is a paper column on the right.
options.risk: Dark green and brass is where many premium restaurants already land, so it can feel familiar.

options.label: The glass wall
options.lineage: A glazier’s black-bar partition, one pane lit
options.thesis: The menu is a wall of glass. One pane lights up for the dish that matters now.
options.viewport: Black mullions divide the first screen into panes. The address is one clear pane. The chosen dish floods one pane. The rest of the menu is a row of quiet panes.
options.case: Clearer for reading one fact per pane. A workshop wall is not how a Columbus diner pictures this restaurant.
options.risk: Elegant and strict, and a little cold for a meal.

options.label: The silk canopy
options.lineage: Overlapping indigo, madder, and saffron banners
options.viewport: Color banners cross a bright courtyard.
options.risk: Beautiful, and hard to read a menu through.
options.case: A diner does not see their dinner in computational silk, and the chords fight the prices.
options.kept: Color is the structure. The oven opening is now a full field that changes with the dish.

options.label: The pop sleeve
options.viewport: One saturated ground, a cropped photo, four titles in a corner.
options.risk: A sleeve is a closed set of four tracks. This menu is not.
options.case: The owner and the diner do not meet on a pop cover, and eight dishes will not fit the corner.
options.kept: One unbroken ground, and a short ranked list instead of a card grid.

options.label: The starburst diner
options.viewport: A cantilever sign, boomerang counter, atomic prices.
options.risk: It sells coffee at the space age, not a premium Indian table.
options.case: The costume argues with the restaurant the owner wants to be proud of.
options.kept: The name and the way in are built at sign scale.

options.label: The night instruments
options.viewport: Six gauges for facts that are not confirmed yet.
options.risk: Dials would pretend the blank hours are a precise reading.
options.case: A pilot’s panel is not dinner, and unconfirmed hours must not look certain.
options.kept: Each unconfirmed fact gets one calm place and shows that it is not confirmed.

options.label: The miniature room
options.viewport: A dollhouse room with a diary beside it.
options.risk: Pastel and tiny. It fights a rich dining room.
options.case: Decorating a room does not help someone choose a table on Macon Road.
options.kept: The visit section is a place you orient in, not a form.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The restaurant page this category already ships, played straight.
canonCard.viewport: A split hero: serif headline on the left, a dish on the right, three equal photo cards under it, then hours.
canonCard.risk: It will look like the prototype you already have, and like every other restaurant site.
